native_result.query: How does the median wealth of white individuals compare to that of black and Hispanic individuals from 1985 onwards?
native_result.HypoA: 1985 onwards, white individuals have a significantly higher median wealth compared to black and Hispanic individuals.
native_result.HypoB:
Main analysis executed as green-lit. Executed script: analysis.py (reproducible, re-run verified). All figures in nominal dollars, unweighted, from data/nls_raw.csv (N=12,686).

## 1. Median family net wealth, available-case, by group × year
| Group | 1985 | 1990 | 1996 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Black (code 1) | $1,600 (n=1,699) | $4,800 (n=1,528) | $9,800 (n=1,368) |
| Hispanic (code 2) | $500 (n=2,631) | $1,600 (n=2,431) | $2,562 (n=2,114) |
| White = code 3 (non-Black, non-Hispanic) | $3,500 (n=5,774) | $12,972 (n=5,336) | $42,600 (n=3,557) |

Median ratios vs. code 3:
| Group | 1985 | 1990 | 1996 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Black / White | 0.457 | 0.370 | 0.230 |
| Hispanic / White | 0.143 | 0.123 | 0.060 |

## 2. Listwise-complete robustness (all three waves present; n=5,739)
| Group | 1985 | 1990 | 1996 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Black (n=1,084) | $1,600 | $4,100 | $9,075 |
| Hispanic (n=1,723) | $300 | $1,200 | $2,400 |
| White = code 3 (n=2,932) | $3,800 | $14,750 | $42,600 |

Listwise ratios — Black/White: 0.421 / 0.278 / 0.213; Hispanic/White: 0.079 / 0.081 / 0.056.

**Direction check:** for all six group×year cells, (group median − white median) is negative under both available-case and listwise (e.g., Black 1996: −$32,800 available-case vs −$33,525 listwise). **The listwise check does not change the direction of any gap** — it only widens the 1990 gaps modestly (the non-Black/non-Hispanic respondents who dropped out before 1996 skew lower-wealth, lifting the 1990 code-3 median from $12,972 to $14,750). The 1996 code-3 median is identical ($42,600) in both specifications.

## 3. Differential attrition note
Non-Black/non-Hispanic non-missing counts fall 5,336 → 3,557 (−33%) from 1990→1996, versus −10.5% for Black (1,528→1,368) and −13% for Hispanic (2,431→2,114). This is the main threat to the 1996 "white" estimate; the listwise result above shows the gap directions and the 1996 code-3 median are robust to it, though the 1990 code-3 level is sensitive.

## 4. Hypothesis (final deliverable, caveats included up front)
**Hypothesis:** From 1985 onwards, the median family net wealth of "white" NLSY79 respondents — proxied by racial/ethnic cohort code 3, NON-BLACK NON-HISPANIC, which also includes other non-Black, non-Hispanic races, so the "white" median is likely diluted and the true white–Black gap understated — was consistently and substantially higher than that of Black and Hispanic respondents in every wave measured (1985, 1990, 1996): nominal medians of $3,500 (1985), $12,972 (1990), and $42,600 (1996) for code 3, versus $1,600/$4,800/$9,800 for Black and $500/$1,600/$2,562 for Hispanic. The Black median was 46% of the code-3 median in 1985, falling to 37% in 1990 and 23% in 1996; the Hispanic median was 14%, 12%, and 6% respectively — i.e., the gap widened over the 1985–1996 window. Note that the wealth measure is family-level net wealth as reported by each individual (co-resident respondents share the same family value), so these are medians of family wealth across individuals in each group, not household-level or per-capita wealth; values are nominal dollars, unweighted, for the NLSY79 young-adult cohort (ages 14–22 in 1979). The finding is robust to the differential 1990→1996 attrition in the non-Black/non-Hispanic group (−33% of 1990 respondents missing in 1996, vs −10.5% Black and −13% Hispanic): a listwise-complete check (n=5,739) reverses the direction of no gap and keeps the 1996 code-3 median at $42,600.

## Limitations
- "White" = code 3 proxy (includes other races); no separate white variable in the file.
- Family-level wealth; individual-level median ≠ household-level median; not divided by family size.
- Nominal dollars, no inflation adjustment; cross-year levels affected by inflation, within-year group comparisons not.
- Unweighted; describes the NLSY79 sample, not the full US population.
- Differential, non-nested attrition across waves; 1996 estimates rest on 55.5% of the sample (3,557 code-3 respondents).
- No wealth data after 1996 in this file, so "1985 onwards" covers exactly 1985/1990/1996.
